display.purpose: Login hero headline only ('Home MCPs'). Never a section heading.

wordmark.purpose: Persistent header brand mark - Anton at 16-18px, uppercase, tight tracking. Distinct from Display, not a scale step.

headline.purpose: Reserved 32px Inter step; not yet drawn on by any current screen.

title.purpose: Every in-app section <h2> - the actual day-to-day heading weight.

label.purpose: Status text and secondary metadata rows.

caption.purpose: Fine print - timestamps, hints, code-block URL text.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Full-pill primary action - form submits, login CTA, key generation.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--color-ink); color: var(--color-on-primary); font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.5; height: 48px; padding: 0 24px; border: none; border-radius: 9999px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-ink); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Destructive Text Button
components.description: No fill, no border - text-only action for Supprimer/Revoquer.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost-destructive { background: none; border: none; color: var(--color-error); font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.5; padding: 4px 8px; margin: -4px -8px; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-ghost-destructive:hover { text-decoration: underline; } .ds-btn-ghost-destructive:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-error); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Placeholder-as-label field - no separate <label> element exists on any current form.
components.css: .ds-input { background: var(--color-soft-cloud); color: var(--color-ink); font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; padding: 8px 12px; border: none; border-radius: 24px; outline: none; width: 100%; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--color-mute); } .ds-input:focus { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--color-ink); }

components.name: Card / Section
components.description: Sharp-cornered, hairline-bordered container - the only container shape in the system.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--color-canvas); border: 1px solid var(--color-hairline); border-radius: 0; padding: 24px; } .ds-card-title { color: var(--color-ink); font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 24px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.2; margin: 0; }

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Active state is a 2px ink underline; inactive is mute text on a transparent underline.
components.html: CredentialsCles API
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; gap: 18px; } .ds-nav-link { font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--color-mute); text-decoration: none; padding-bottom: 4px; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; } .ds-nav-link:hover { color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-nav-link--active { color: var(--color-ink); border-bottom-color: var(--color-ink); }

components.name: Status Label
components.description: Text-only status indicator - no chip/background, color alone carries state.
components.css: .ds-status-label { font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.5; } .ds-status-label--success { color: var(--color-success); } .ds-status-label--error { color: var(--color-error); } .ds-status-label--warning { color: var(--color-warning); }

narrative.overview: This is not a product being sold to strangers - it is personal infrastructure, visited briefly and rarely, whose entire job is custody: storing credentials for services that don't offer a clean way to be reached by an MCP client, and minting the API keys that let a client reach them. Every decision in this system serves that framing. There is no brand accent color because there is nothing to sell; the palette is Carbon & Paper - near-black ink on white and off-white paper, the same restraint as a receipt or a ledger, not a screen-native gradient world. Where the system does allow itself softness - the full-pill buttons, the 24px-radius inputs - it reads as approachable rather than decorative: Soft and approachable controls sitting inside sharp, flat, hairline-bordered containers. The one deliberately loud gesture is the Anton wordmark, used at two completely different scales (a tiny uppercase brand mark in the header, a massive 64px campaign headline on login) and nowhere else - display type is rationed, not a general-purpose headline font.
keyCharacteristics: Fully neutral palette: no brand hue, only ink/canvas/soft-cloud grays plus three semantic status colors (success/error/warning).
Flat by construction: zero shadows anywhere in the implementation; depth comes from a two-step background lightness (soft-cloud page -> canvas card) plus 1px hairline borders.
Two-register shape language: structural containers (cards, code blocks) are sharp (0px radius); every interactive control (buttons, inputs) is heavily rounded (24px inputs, full-pill buttons).
Display type (Anton) is rationed to exactly two roles - the persistent brand wordmark and the login hero headline - never a general section-heading font.
Single breakpoint: sm (640px) is the only responsive boundary used anywhere in the app.
Dark mode is a first-class, system-driven inversion of the same neutral family (off-black/off-white, never pure), not a separate design.

rules.name: The No-Accent Rule
rules.body: There is no brand color. Every non-neutral pixel in this system is a semantic status color (success/error/warning) carrying real state, never decoration. Introducing a brand accent is a product decision, not a styling one - it would contradict "The Utility Vault" framing.

rules.name: The Dark Mode Is Not Optional Rule
rules.body: Every color token ships a dark counterpart, driven purely by prefers-color-scheme (no manual toggle exists). A new token without a dark value is an incomplete token, not a follow-up.

rules.name: The Rationed Display Rule
rules.body: Anton appears in exactly two places on any screen: the persistent header wordmark and (on /login only) the hero headline. It is never a general section-heading font - every <h2> in the authenticated app is Inter Title, not Anton.

rules.name: The Single Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: sm (640px) is the only responsive boundary in the app. There is no md/lg/xl behavior anywhere - a screen is either "narrow" or "not narrow."

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never cast shadows. If a future component needs elevation, express it as another background-lightness step plus a hairline border, not a box-shadow.

rules.name: The Structure-vs-Action Rule
rules.body: If it holds content, it's sharp. If you can click, type into, or press it, it's heavily rounded. A rounded card or a sharp-cornered button would both be off-system.

dos: Do keep Anton rationed to the header wordmark and the login hero - never use it for an in-app section heading (Title / Inter / 24px owns that job).
Do pair every new color token with its dark-mode counterpart in the same change - dark mode is system-driven and always-on, not an opt-in surface.
Do keep structural containers sharp and interactive controls rounded - the two registers are the system's shape language, not an inconsistency to reconcile.
Do collapse a content+action row to flex-col below sm whenever the row can plausibly overflow on a narrow viewport - the credential cards and API key rows already establish this pattern.
Do use a plain colored status word for state, not a background pill/badge - matches the existing Status Label pattern.
donts: Don't introduce a brand accent color. The No-Accent Rule is deliberate, not an oversight to fix.
Don't add box-shadow anywhere. Depth is background-lightness + hairline border only.
Don't add a second responsive breakpoint (md/lg/xl) without a concrete layout that needs it - the app has stayed on a single sm boundary by design, not by omission.
Don't round a card/container or sharpen a button/input - it breaks the Structure-vs-Action Rule and reads as an inconsistency, not a variation.
